text:
maya: Heads-up — canary deploy (canary-id: c-20260318-08) is at 10% in us-west1 and were seeing a KV mismatch: stale prefix lookup -> user 502s up 4%. Holding the rollout. Need a clear fast-revert + safe-disable plan that handles cache/KV without causing thundering herd.

kevin: Agreed. My suggested procedure (short):
1) Freeze traffic split (stop further increases).
2) Flip routing health for canary -> mark unhealthy so router immediately diverts to baseline.
3) Invalidate problematic KV prefixes in-region (staged).
4) Toggle cache-safe header/flag to bypass for 1 minute while KV stabilizes.
5) Bump telemetry sampling and enable detailed traces for affected routes.
I'll paste the API calls.

kevin: API commands (control-plane):
```bash
# set traffic for rollout id to 0% canary, 100% baseline
curl -X PATCH "https://control.internal.redwood/v1/rollouts/c-20260318-08/traffic" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"splits": [{"variant":"baseline","weight":1.0},{"variant":"canary","weight":0.0}] }'

# mark canary unhealthy in routing policy
curl -X POST "https://control.internal.redwood/v1/routing/canary-mark" -d '{"canary_id":"c-20260318-08","healthy":false}'
```

kevin: KV invalidation (careful): prefer staged prefix touch vs global flush. Example: set a tombstone key that makes runtime treat prefix as stale, then let workers lazily evict.
```bash
# tombstone marker approach (per-region)
curl -X POST "https://control.internal.redwood/v1/kv/markers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"region":"us-west1","prefix":"/models/c-20260318-08/","marker":"tombstone","ttl_sec":60}'
```

ops-bot: Executing traffic patch: PATCH /v1/rollouts/c-20260318-08/traffic — success (200). Routing flag updated (canary -> unhealthy).

sophie: Quick Q — tombstone approach spreads load but still risks many clients refetching. Another option: set runtime "cache-bypass" header or short-circuit routing to baseline until KV warm-up completes. If we set cache-bypass, make sure downstream L7 proxies respect `x-redwood-cache: bypass`.

kevin: Yes. Toggle header via runtime config for the affected route for 90s:
```json
{ "route_id": "/v1/generate", "runtime_overrides": { "response_cache_mode": "bypass", "override_ttl": 90 } }
```
Apply per-region to avoid global blast.

ryan: From UX/console side: we should add an "Abort rollout + Invalidate cache" quick action that does both steps above (PATCH traffic + create marker). Backend endpoint could be `POST /internal/rollouts/{id}/abort?invalidate=true`. I'll open a small ticket.

kevin: Also: bump trace sampling for `canary_id` header and add p50/p95/5xx guards so we have better telemetry during the window. Example alert thresholds: p95 latency > 2s OR 5xx rate > 1% -> auto rollback (if enabled).

maya: Doing staged tombstone per-region now (us-west1). Will monitor error-rate and token/hit patterns. Thanks for the command snippets.

ops-bot: KV marker created in us-west1. Tombstone key: `/markers/c-20260318-08/tombstone` ttl=60.

sophie: One ops note — when you add tombstone, also stagger the worker eviction window (10s offsets) so the backend doesn't rehydration spike at once.

kevin: Good call. We'll run staggered TTLs (60, 70, 80s) and keep rollback live for 15m before full investigate. Posting runbook link: https://wiki.internal.redwood/runbooks/rollouts#canary-kv-rollback

maya: Marking thread resolved once metrics flatten. Will follow-up with postmortem if we need a change to rollout guards.

kevin: Follow-up action items: (a) make `abort+invalidate` console action ticket, (b) add runtime flag to disable prefix caching quickly, (c) add automatic staged-markers to the fast-revert playbook.

ryan: Filed console ticket ENG-4891.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
